draft.title: The Nazi rise to power
card: The Great Depression hit Germany from 1929. Millions lost their jobs, and many Germans lost faith in the Weimar government. The Nazi Party, which had won few votes in the 1920s, gained far more support.
In 1932 the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag, Germany's parliament. They never won a majority in a free election.
In January 1933 President Hindenburg appointed Hitler chancellor. Conservative leaders hoped they could control him.
In March 1933 the Reichstag passed the Enabling Act. It let Hitler's government make laws without the Reichstag, so he could rule as a dictator.
draft.remember: Depression support brought Hitler the chancellorship. The Enabling Act gave him dictatorial power.

a.q: How did Hitler come to hold the office of chancellor in January 1933?
opts: President Hindenburg appointed him
He won a majority of seats in a free election
He took power by force in a coup
The Reichstag passed the Enabling Act
a.why: Hindenburg, the president, appointed Hitler after the Nazis became the largest party. The Nazis never won a majority in a free election. The Enabling Act came later, in March 1933, and gave Hitler the power to make laws.
a.clue: Think about who had the power to name a chancellor.

b.q: Which statement best explains why the Enabling Act mattered for Hitler's power?
opts: It let his government make laws without the Reichstag
It made him chancellor for the first time
It gave the Nazis their first seats in parliament
It ended the Great Depression in Germany
b.why: The Act let the government pass laws without the Reichstag, which is what allowed Hitler to rule as a dictator. It did not make him chancellor, because Hindenburg had already appointed him in January 1933. That appointment is the tempting wrong answer.
b.clue: Check the order of events: the Act came after Hitler became chancellor.

b.best: It let his government make laws without the Reichstag

problems.detail: 'Depression support brought Hitler the chancellorship' makes the link neater than the card does. The card says Hindenburg appointed him and that conservative leaders hoped to control him, so popular support alone did not make him chancellor. Something like 'Depression support made the Nazis the largest party; Hindenburg then appointed Hitler chancellor' would match the card and question a.
